title: Selective Detection of Female Sex Pheromone of _Helicoverpa armigera_ by an Eminent Surface Functionalized Template
protocol: Clean a silicon wafer with piranha solution for 5 minutes.
Wash the silicon wafer repeatedly with distilled water to remove contaminants.
Thermally grow a 1 μm layer of silicon dioxide over the cleaned wafer by nano pyrogenic furnace.
Dehydrate the properly cleaned wafer at 250 ºC for 10 minutes on a hot plate.
Spin coat the wafer with AZ5214E photoresist to achieve a thickness of approximately 1.5 μm at 6000 rpm for 40 seconds.
Bake the coated wafer at 110 ºC for 2 minutes to evaporate solvents in the photoresist.
Fix a 3 inch DRIE lithomask over the treated wafer.
Expose the mask to UV light for 2 seconds at 50 millijoules/cm² in an EVG 620 double-sided mask aligner.
Develop the mask by dipping it in AZ351B:H₂O solution (ratio 1:4) for 30 seconds.
Wash the developed mask with distilled water and dry it under nitrogen.
Heat the dried mask at 110°C for 4 minutes to obtain the pattern for microstructures.
Observe the developed cantilevers and fixed-fixed beams under an optical microscope.
Place formalin oil on a large carrier wafer to create a sticky base for the sample.
Load the sample into the reactive ion etching chlorine (RIE-Cl) chamber.
Plasma etch silicon dioxide (SiO₂) with 5 torr pressure and 50 power for 6 minutes.
Etch silicon isotropically with 7.5 torr pressure and 30 power for 3 minutes.
Remove photoresist by oxygen etching at 0 torr pressure and 150 power for 4 minutes.
Clean the surfaces of silicon dioxide based substrates by dipping in 20 mL piranha solution (H₂SO₄:H₂O₂ = 9:1) for 5 min.
Maintain the temperature of the piranha solution at 85°C.
Add H₂O₂ carefully to replenish the temperature.
Remove organic and metallic contaminants from the surfaces.
Proceed with further functionalization steps after cleaning.
Functionalize hydroxyl groups on cleaned substrate surfaces with 4% 3-aminopropyl triethoxy silane in toluene under N₂ atmosphere at room temperature for 2 hours.
Rinse the functionalized surfaces repeatedly with distilled water.
Dry the surfaces under a nitrogen flow.
Functionalize hydroxyl groups on cleaned substrate surfaces with 10% 3-mercaptopropyl triethoxy silane in toluene under N₂ atmosphere at room temperature for 4 hours.
Rinse the functionalized surfaces repeatedly with fresh toluene.
Dry the surfaces under a nitrogen flow.
React free thiol groups on the surfaces with 3-(maleimido)-propionic acid N-hydroxysuccinimide ester in DMF for 5 hours.
Rinse the reacted surfaces properly with water and ethanol.
Dry the surfaces under a nitrogen flow.
React surface-immobilized N-hydroxysuccinimido group with amino-functionalized polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (POSS-NH₂) in a DMF:H₂O mixture of 3:1.
Add ten equivalents of triethylamine (Et₃N) and 0.1 equivalent of dimethylaminopyridine (DMAP) to the reaction mixture.
Keep the reaction mixture overnight at room temperature.
Rinse the reacted surface with distilled water repeatedly.
Dry the surface under a nitrogen flow.
React the aminated surface with 10% glutaraldehyde in PBS buffer (pH 7.4) for 4 hours at room temperature.
Wash the surface with distilled water after the reaction.
Dry the surface under a nitrogen flow.
Clean surfaces for atomic force microscopy.
Glue cleaned surfaces over a plate using double-sided tape.
Record images using silicon AFM tip with a resonance frequency of about 300 kHz and a force constant of 40 N/m.
Acquire data using a focused 30KV Ga ion source in the LMIG gun.
Raster the ion source over a 300 × 300 μm area to induce desorption and ionization of species from the surface.
Maintain beam current at approximately 7 nA during acquisition.
Accelerate secondary ions into the mass spectrometer for mass separation.
Record mass spectra in positive ion mode with a range of 0-1500 amu.
Acquire surface spectra on 3-5 sections, each lasting 5 minutes, per sample set.
Generate a 2D image by rastering a finely focused ion beam across the sample surface.
Collect advanced 3-D dynamic response data from functionalized MEMS devices using MSA-500 instruments before and after pheromone attachment.
Measure the resonant frequency due to base vibration with a laser doppler vibrometer (LDV).
Quantify change in displacement and velocity of vibrating structures without surface contact using LDV.
Extract measured resonant frequency by analyzing vibration spectrum with polytech acquisition software.
